raw_content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "longitudinal_cxr_progression_assessment", "description": "When assessing disease progression across multiple chest X-rays using an uncalibrated classifier, do not rely on small score deltas to determine severity changes.", "applicable_conditions": "Tasks involving the comparison of two or more chest X-rays to determine spatial or severity progression of findings (e.g., pneumonia, edema, effusion) where a probabilistic classifier is available but not calibrated for absolute severity quantification.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": ["chest_xray_classifier"], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "If comparing longitudinal chest X-rays: (1) Use `chest_xray_classifier` only to confirm the presence of strong findings (score > high threshold) in each image independently; (2) Do NOT interpret minor score differences (e.g., 0.88 vs 0.89) as clinical progression or regression; (3) Rely on direct visual inspection of pixel evidence across timepoints to identify spatial changes (e.g., new opacities, contralateral spread, volume loss) for determining true progression."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
